interpretation: The existing checked MPPI near-prefix was actually used, and the new reference was actually adopted.
The prefix and final B candidate pass on the same side as MPPI in this trial; initialization is not an execution commitment.
Real delivery improved in this pair, but the resulting native reference became wider and slower; overall navigation performance did not uniformly improve.
Actual B crossing closely follows the wider native output, so this is not merely extra MPPI tracking deviation.
The early-delivery backend exits at its first feasible candidate; this run does not establish that further iterations would fix the quality regression.
No particular cost weight, wheel constraint or budget is asserted to be the isolated cause of route widening without further evidence.
Single asynchronous A/B is neither identical-input nor statistical performance proof.
Exact handover timing, stable general-case delivery and dual-timescale coupled optimization remain unresolved.
